components.cost_effect: One response observation for each update.
components.goal: Move the estimate toward the regression root without evaluating M or its derivative.
components.key_estimate: With b_n=E[(x_n-theta)^2], d_n=E[(x_n-theta)(M(x_n)-alpha)] and e_n=E[(y_n-alpha)^2], Eq.(14) gives b_{n+1}-b_n=a_n^2 e_n-2a_n d_n.
components.name: Response-residual feedback
components.operation: Observe y_n at x_n and add a_n(alpha-y_n).
components.requires: The prescribed response kernel and the linked theorem's boundedness, monotonicity and local derivative conditions for consistency.
transfer_checks: Reestablish drift and noise control after changing response assumptions, gain sequence, dimension, update or output.

limitations.statement: Theorem 2 gives no finite-time epsilon-complexity or optimality result. Immediately after it the authors explicitly leave replacing bounded observations by their proposed bounded-mean/bounded-variance condition unresolved.

performance_links.scope_note: The a/n subclass of the full type-1/n Theorem 2 statement; mean-square convergence only.

variants.cost: One response observation per update. The displayed scalar subtraction, multiplication, addition and gain evaluation require constant arithmetic per update; current-state storage is constant in the real-arithmetic interpretation. These are bookkeeping descriptions of the displayed recursion, not source bit-complexity bounds. Response-generation cost and numerical precision are unspecified and must be charged separately in an implementation.
variants.implementation_details_ref: printed p.401, Eq.(7)–(8); printed p.404, Eq.(30); printed p.405, Theorem 2
variants.name: Robbins–Monro scalar recursion with a_n=a/n
variants.output: The current iterate x_n as estimator of theta; x_n uses n-1 response observations.
public_inputs: Known finite target alpha; chosen finite deterministic x_1; chosen gain constant a>0.
variants.query_and_update: Query at x_n for one scalar response y_n with conditional CDF H(.|x_n); set x_{n+1}=x_n+(a/n)(alpha-y_n), then increment n. No projection, averaging or derivative query appears in Eq.(7)–(8).
variants.requirements: Real-valued query levels. At each x_n obtain the response under the paper's Markov sampling rule H(.|x_n). For the linked guarantee: a common finite C>0 bounds |Y(x)| almost surely for every real x; M(x)=E[Y(x)] is nondecreasing, M(theta)=alpha, and the ordinary derivative at theta exists and is positive.
variants.state_and_initialization: Set n=1 and x=x_1. Maintain current scalar x_n and iteration counter. Theta, H, M and M'(theta) need not be known to execute the recursion.
variants.tuning_and_stopping: Any fixed a>0 gives the sufficient Eq.(30) subclass. Choose a finite iteration budget to run; the selected theorem supplies asymptotic convergence, not an accuracy-certified stopping rule or optimal gain.

use_restrictions: Asymptotic performance of this specified algorithm, not unrestricted Oracle Complexity.

title: Robbins–Monro scalar stochastic approximation
use_when: Estimate a monotone scalar regression root from sequential bounded responses; do not substitute a bounded-variance-only model.
